exact_items: `OpenCode_Deep_Extraction.md` source-verifies hard architecture limits: server-global SSE with concurrent-client pollution, fixed server working directory requiring separate instances per worktree, session-scoped approvals and compaction state that are destroyed on session deletion, no observable upstream account identity, and no real reconnect/observe path for mid-run SSE loss.
These should not be collapsed back into generic summary language during reconciliation.
notes: OpenCode_Deep_Extraction.md must formally document five hard architecture limits as PM-side constraints requiring explicit scoping logic: (1) server-global SSE with concurrent-client pollution, (2) fixed server working directory (separate instances per worktree), (3) session-scoped approvals/compaction lost on session deletion, (4) no observable upstream account identity, (5) no reconnect/observe path for mid-run SSE loss.

exact_items: The contract now has enough shape to define concrete route normalization for the most common user-facing flows.

cost usage -> Show in Usage: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=usage_event`, `object_id=<canonical usage event id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread-scoped, `inspector_target=usage`
cost usage -> Show in Ledger: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=usage_event`, `object_id=<id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread-scoped, `tab_id=ledger`

wizard resume: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=wizard`, `object_id=<wizard_id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread must be restored; serialized `resume_url` carries narrow step anchor detail
chat search hit: `target_kind=side_panel`, `project_id=<id>`, `thread_id=<id>`, `object_kind=message`, `object_id=<message_id>`

node detail pivot: `target_kind=page_tab`, `project_id=<id>`, `focused_run_id=<run_id>`, `object_kind=node`, `object_id=<node_id>`, `tab_id=node_graph`, `inspector_target=details|evidence|usage|history`
notes: Contracts_V0.md should include concrete route normalization examples for the five highest-pressure user flows: (1) Show in Usage, (2) Show in Ledger, (3) Wizard Resume, (4) Chat Search Hit, (5) Node Detail Pivot. These serve as canonical worked examples that confirm the bounded field set is correct.
